amendments.before: any rerank request for a study query (only first-stage pools had been computed)
amendments.finding: For all 360 queries the hybrid fused top 40 has exactly the membership of the dense top 40 (pools-check.json: union size 40 for every query, no lexical-only row). At lexical weight 0.5 a lexical-only candidate scores at most 0.5/61 = 0.0082, below the 1/(60+40) = 0.0100 of the 40th vector candidate, so outside the exact-lookup tier (two or three content terms, all matched) the lexical leg can only reorder the vector top 40, never add to it. No study query triggered the tier.
changes: The hybrid40, dense40 and union pools are one candidate set. Reranked arms are reported once, over that set (scores from one 40-document request per query in chunk-id order); dense40 and union rerank arms would repeat it and are dropped. The first-stage arms hybrid and dense remain: they order the same 40 chunks differently.

The union-score replay question disappears: the scored request is already the 40-document pool. The verification sample keeps its 50 queries but changes its requests: every reranker gets the same 40 documents in fused (production) order, which measures uncached latency and tests whether document order changes scores; ali-qwen3-rerank additionally gets the first 20 documents of that order, which tests whether scores depend on the other documents in the request (the documented request-relative caveat). The dense40 direct request, which would now duplicate the scored request, is dropped.
Candidate recall of the shared pool (relevant excerpt among the 40 chunks) is reported as the ceiling every arm shares.
